Additionally, the return on assets (ROA) is only 1.18%, well below the sector average of 22.62% [E8] and even lower than the median ROA of -1% over the last three years [E28]. This implies that the company's asset utilization efficiency is subpar, raising concerns about its ability to generate sustainable profits. In summary, while profitability metrics are concerning, they do not necessarily outweigh the strong sales and profit growth trends observed in the company. The valuation metrics, particularly P/B, suggest potential undervaluation relative to book value.

Lastly, while the bull points out recent profit growth of 30.6% CAGR over the last five years [E60], this does not negate the negative ROE trends. The evidence shows that median return on equity has been low or negative for Indsil, suggesting that the company's profitability is a concern that cannot be ignored.
